title: A Frontend user whose address is not already saved reaches a dead end on every address-selection page; Design release 1 offers a route to add a new address on all of them and returns the user with the new address chosen

finding.frontend: On any of Frontend's five consignment party pickers, a search that matches nothing renders one line — "No addresses match your search." — and nothing else: no link, no button, no guidance (fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-no-matches). The only control left is "Save and continue", and submitting without a row selected returns "Select a consignor from the list" in an error summary (fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter-error), so the page cannot be satisfied at all. The picker form is a search input, a Search button, the results table, its pagination and Save and continue, and nothing more (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-113); the addresses feature's copy holds no add-an-address key at all, the empty state's only string being noMatches (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:43-62). The contact-address page is a different shape — the whole book as thirteen radios rather than a search — but it is the same dead end: it offers no way to add an address either (fe-contact). Searching the rendered DOM of every one of the 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "add a new address", "add an address" or "address book" returns nothing. So a trader whose place of origin has never been saved cannot finish the addresses section, and the service gives them no way to find that out except by failing.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 gives every address-selection page a route out to add one. On the five party pickers it is a secondary "Add a new address" button sitting under the results table and above "Save and continue" — six captured screens carry it, the five picker headings plus the search-filtered state — pointing at /address-book/add?from=<section> (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:162-163, with the href built at app/routes.js:3598-3600). On the contact-address page it is worded differently and sits above the radios, as a link inside the sentence "If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.", pointing at /address-book/add?from=contact-address. Following either skips the address-type chooser, because the section the user came from implies the type and is carried in a hidden addressType, and lands on "Add address details" (dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker), where the address can be searched for or typed in by hand. Saving writes the address to the book, selects it into the section the user came from, redirects them back to that same page and shows a success message naming the address just added (app/routes.js:8118-8194). The notification is never abandoned.
finding.difference: Give every address-selection page a route out, and a return path back to it with the new address selected — the five pickers and the contact-address page. Nothing has to land first: the address-book API behind Frontend already serves create, and every other part of the picker exists. What a person has to choose is the destination, and it is the same choice this run's scope question turns on (address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent) — either an add-address page inside this frontend, which means giving its address-book service a write path it deliberately does not have (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19), or a link out to the Import Notification Service front door's existing /address-book/add, which needs a return URL so the user comes back to the page they left rather than being stranded in another service's address book. The empty state's copy is part of the work either way: "No addresses match your search." is a statement with no next step in it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any link or button on a Frontend party picker or the contact-address page that leads to adding an address.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier: grepped all 67 captured Frontend DOM files for "add a new address", "add an address" and "address-book" — no match anywhere, and reading fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-no-matches.html end to end shows the form holds only the crumb, the page field, the q input, the Search button, the noMatches paragraph and Save and continue. Opened fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-no-matches.png, dr1-consignment-address-select.png and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment.png. Checked rubric 1 rather than taking the dead end on the page's word: fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter-error.html carries "There is a problem" and "Select a consignor from the list" both in the error summary and inline, so the picker is mandatory and the claim is about the journey, not only the markup — it stands. Checked both DR1 citations at the cited lines: app/views/consignment-address-select.html:161-165 is the govukButton and app/routes.js:3598-3600 is the addAddressHref ternary, both root-mount, and read saveAddressBookEntry at app/routes.js:8118-8194 to confirm the write, the section sync, the success message and the redirect back to consignmentReturn.path. Confirmed "Add a new address" appears exactly once on dr1-consignment-address-select.html, so the crop resolves. Rubric 2 fired on the prototype slot — see correction.
finding.correction: The author wrote that Design release 1 "puts a secondary 'Add a new address' button under the results table on all five party pickers and on the contact-address page — seven captured screens carry it". The button claim is right for the pickers and wrong for the contact-address page. Grepping the prototype capture for "Add a new address" returns eight files: the six consignment-address-select screens (the five picker headings plus the search-filtered state), dr1-address-book.html, where it is the list page's own primary button, and dr1-address-book-add.html, where it is a caption above the heading rather than a button at all. dr1-contact-address-for-consignment.html is not among them: it carries the link "add a new branch address" at line 269 of the captured DOM, inside a sentence above the radios, and the screenshot shows it as body copy rather than a button. The underlying claim — that Design release 1 offers a route to add an address where Frontend offers none — holds on that page too, and the href is the same /address-book/add?from= shape, so the slot has been corrected rather than narrowed: the count is now six picker screens, the contact page's own wording and placement are stated, and fe-contact and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment have been added to screens with "add a new branch address" added to controls so that page's card crops its own control. The title was widened from "every picker" to "every address-selection page" to match. The falsifier's second sentence, which asserted the picker DOM carries only five things, has been dropped: the error state also carries an error summary, and the first sentence is the falsifier. Note for the cross-slice sweep: fe-contact, dr1-contact-address-for-consignment and dr1-consignment-address-select belong to the addresses slice in slices.json, so this finding reaches across the boundary by design — the address-book slice note licenses it, but a duplicate from the addresses author is possible.

relatedTo.why: Where the button leads depends on whether Design release 1's eight address-book pages are this frontend's work; the button itself is needed either way.
